s: Lease-based mutual exclusion across processes/nodes so exactly-one-worker runs critical sections safely.
w: Acquire writes a lock key with TTL lease + fencing token (monotonic id). Holders renew leases while working; expiry auto-releases crashed holders. Fencing tokens let downstream resources reject stale holders' writes after lease loss. Backends range from redis (SET NX PX) to zookeeper/etcd consensus for stronger guarantees.
use: Singleton cron deduplication across replica instances
Resource arbitration (one indexer scans shard X now)
avoid: High-frequency coordination (>thousands/sec - redesign to sharding/token buckets)
Correctness-critical mutual exclusion on plain redis without fencing (split-brain risks)

pat.d: Locks elect leaders implicitly; election formalizes it.

pits: GC pause exceeding lease = two holders - fencing tokens REQUIRED for safety-critical sections
Clock jumps breaking TTL math - prefer monotonic-source-backed stores
tips: Know Kleppmann's Redlock critique - fencing tokens argument separates deep from shallow answers
